title: Analytics & Visualization – New Notes
subtitle: Warehouses, lakes, lakehouses, ETL/ELT, Synapse, Data Factory and Power BI — Chapter 4 revision with exam clues.

what.body: Data analytics turns data into useful information and insights. Modern data platforms collect, prepare, store, analyze and visualize data: operational systems feed ingestion pipelines, which fill lakes and warehouses, where analytics runs and Power BI visualizes the results.
what.example: Five years of sales flow from orders systems and files through Data Factory into a warehouse, where a star schema lets analysts slice revenue by product, region and month — and Power BI turns it into a dashboard answering: which region generates the most revenue?

concepts.body: Examining data to discover information, patterns, trends and insights. Goal: turn data into information that supports decisions. Example questions: which products sell most, which region earns most, which month peaked?

OLTP runs day-to-day operations (place an order: frequent INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on current data, fast individual transactions). OLAP analyzes data (yearly sales: analytical reads and aggregations over historical/integrated data, complex queries).

Centralized analytical store for reporting and BI. Integrates data from multiple operational systems; stores curated, historical data; optimized for analytical queries; keeps analytics off operational systems. Traits: subject-oriented (sales, customers, products), integrated, historical, analytical.
Stores measurable business events/metrics: keys plus numbers like Quantity and SalesAmount. Memory: fact = what you measure.
Stores descriptive context used to slice facts: ProductName, Category, Brand. Memory: dimension = how you describe the measurement.
Central fact table surrounded by dimension tables (date, product, customer dimensions around a sales fact). Simpler dimensions, fewer joins. DP-900 clue: central fact + surrounding dimensions = star.
Like star, but dimensions are further normalized into related tables (Product -> Category -> Department). More normalized, can need more joins.
ETL = Extract, Transform, Load: transform BEFORE loading (traditional warehouse pattern). ELT = Extract, Load, Transform: load first, transform inside the target (common in modern cloud platforms).

Ingestion brings data in from databases, files, APIs, apps, IoT and event systems. Batch = scheduled groups (last night's sales every night). Streaming = continuous, very-low-latency event flow (IoT sensor readings).

Large-scale storage holding raw or relatively raw data of all kinds: structured, semi-structured and unstructured (CSV, JSON, logs, images, video, extracts). Memory: lake = flexible storage for many data types. Often schema-on-read.
Lake flexibility + warehouse-style analytics in one shared platform, serving BI, analytics, data engineering and data science.
Schema-on-write: structure first, then store (transform to fit before/as written). Schema-on-read: store first, interpret later (structure applied when read or analyzed).
A data mart is a smaller analytical store for one area (sales, finance, marketing, HR). Analytics summarizes with SUM/COUNT/AVG, often grouped: SUM(SalesAmount), GROUP BY Region.
Descriptive: what happened? (sales were 10 crore). Diagnostic: why? (supply issues). Predictive: what may happen? (sales may rise). Prescriptive: what should we do? (increase inventory).

concepts.term: Big data 3 Vs and data quality
concepts.body: Volume (large amounts), Velocity (speed of generation/processing), Variety (formats/sources) — plus Veracity and Value. Results depend on quality: watch missing values, duplicates, incorrect/inconsistent/outdated/invalid data; cleanse and transform before analysis.

examples.title: Star schema in one picture
examples.body: A Sales fact (DateKey, ProductKey, CustomerKey, Quantity, SalesAmount) sits in the center; Date, Product and Customer dimensions surround it. Slicing total sales by Brand A vs Brand B joins the fact to the Product dimension.

examples.title: ETL or ELT?
examples.body: Nightly job extracts shop sales, cleans them, then loads the warehouse: ETL (transform before load). IoT JSON lands raw in the lake and Spark SQL reshapes it later: ELT (load first, transform after).

examples.title: End-to-end modern pipeline
examples.body: Operational databases + files + APIs + IoT feed Data Factory ingestion, which fills the Data Lake / Warehouse; Synapse or SQL/Spark analyzes; Power BI reports. Sources -> Ingestion -> Storage -> Transformation -> Analytics -> Visualization.

services.name: Azure Synapse Analytics
services.what: Microsoft analytics service combining enterprise data warehousing, big data analytics and data integration.
services.when: Large-scale Azure analytics and warehousing workloads.
services.scenario: Question says 'large-scale Azure analytics' or enterprise data warehousing.

services.name: Azure Data Factory
services.what: Cloud data-integration service: build pipelines that move and orchestrate data between sources and destinations.
services.when: Copying, scheduling or orchestrating data movement (SQL Database -> pipeline -> lake/warehouse).
services.scenario: Question says 'move/orchestrate data between sources' or mentions pipelines.

services.name: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2
services.what: Azure storage built for large-scale data lake and analytics scenarios, with a hierarchical namespace.
services.data: Structured, semi-structured and unstructured data at scale.
services.when: You need data-lake storage feeding analytics.
services.scenario: Question says 'data lake storage + hierarchical namespace + analytics'.

services.name: Power BI
services.what: Microsoft business analytics and visualization platform: reports, dashboards, charts, interactive visuals.
services.when: Dashboards and visual reports over analyzed data.
services.scenario: Question says 'dashboards/visual reports' — think Power BI.

remember: OLTP runs the business (transactions). OLAP analyzes it (history, aggregations).
Warehouse = curated analytical data from many sources. Lake = raw + curated, all formats.
Fact = measures (quantity, revenue). Dimension = descriptive context (product, region).
Star = fact in center, dimensions around. Snowflake = dimensions further normalized.
ETL = transform BEFORE loading. ELT = load first, transform later.
Batch = scheduled groups. Streaming = continuous event flow.
Schema-on-write = structure first. Schema-on-read = store first, interpret later.
Data Factory = pipelines + integration. Synapse = enterprise analytics. ADLS Gen2 = lake storage. Power BI = visualization.
Descriptive (what) -> Diagnostic (why) -> Predictive (what next) -> Prescriptive (what to do).
3 Vs: Volume, Velocity, Variety. Cleanse data before analysis.

quickCheck.q: Central store of curated historical data for reporting?
quickCheck.a: Data warehouse. Raw multi-format storage = data lake; both combined = lakehouse.

quickCheck.q: Table with Quantity and SalesAmount vs table with ProductName and Brand?
quickCheck.a: First is a fact table (measures); second is a dimension table (descriptive context).

quickCheck.q: Central fact surrounded by dimensions — and its normalized cousin?
quickCheck.a: Star schema; dimensions further normalized into related tables = snowflake schema.

quickCheck.q: Transform before loading or load before transforming?
quickCheck.a: Transform before = ETL (traditional warehouses). Load first = ELT (modern cloud).

quickCheck.q: Nightly sales load vs live IoT sensor feed?
quickCheck.a: Nightly groups = batch. Continuous events = streaming.

quickCheck.q: Move data between sources on a schedule — and visualize the result?
quickCheck.a: Move/orchestrate with Data Factory pipelines; visualize with Power BI dashboards.
